text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- FINANCIAL SYSTEM WILL BE REFORMULATED

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso believes the privatization of state banks, the recovery of private banks and the current investigation into a multi-million-dollar scam involving state and municipal bonds are all part of the same process to reformulate the Brazilian financial system.
-- CVRD PROFIT UP 76 PCT IN 1996
State mining giant CVRD has achieved one of its best results in 1996, with inflation adjusted net profit increasing 76 percent to 632 million reais.
-- BANK NETWORK ADVANCED IN BRAZIL
A Salomon Brothers study shows that Brazil and Mexico have the most advanced banking networks in Latin America and are on a par with Europe and Asia.
O ESTADO DE SAO PAULO
-- WHOLESALE CAR SALES INCREASE 15 PERCENT
February wholesale car sales rose 15 percent on January with 137,817 cars sold. Volkswagen, Fiat, General Motors and Ford were the leading makes.
-- COLD WEATHER CLOTHING TO BE 10 PERCENT CHEAPER

Cold weather clothing will be 10 percent cheaper than last year, according to the Brazilian Clothing Association, because manufacturers used less imported materials and replaced them with less expensive domestic production.
O GLOBO
-- CPI WILL ASK LARGE BANKS TO MAKE STATEMENTS

A special Parliamentary Investigative Committee (CPI) will ask large banks and pension funds to make statements in connection with its inquiries into a multi-million-dollar scam involving state and municipal bonds.
-- NON-ORGAN DONORS WILL HAVE TO ALTER DOCUMENTS

Brazilians over 21 years of age who do not want to donate their organs should they die have to state this on their identity cards or driving license, otherwise their consent to organ donation is assumed automatically.
-- RIO AND BUENOS AIRES SEAL ACCORD FOR 2004 OLYMPICS
Rio de Janeiro and Buenos Aires, both bidders for the 2004 Olympic Games, have agreed to back each other should one of them not be among the five finalists to be announced tomorrow.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
